title: Search for stable hadronising squarks and gluinos with the ATLAS experiment at the LHC
extended_summary:
This paper reports a particle-physics search at the ATLAS experiment for slow-moving, long-lived colored supersymmetric particles that would hadronize into so-called R-hadrons. The central question is whether proton-proton collisions at the LHC produce stable or metastable squarks and gluinos that can be detected through unusual ionization loss and time-of-flight signatures.

The study uses 34 pb−1 of 7 TeV proton-proton collision data from the ATLAS detector. Candidate events are selected with a missing-transverse-energy trigger and then filtered using tracks with high transverse momentum, pixel-detector dE/dx measurements, and tile-calorimeter time-of-flight estimates to reconstruct candidate mass. Backgrounds are estimated with data-driven methods, and signal efficiencies are evaluated using Monte Carlo simulation under several R-hadron interaction models.

The work is not an educational intervention study, so it has no student or educator population. Its main conclusion is that no deviation from Standard Model expectations is observed, leading to 95% confidence-level exclusion limits on stable sbottoms, stops, and gluinos. The most conservative lower mass limits reported are 294 GeV for sbottoms, 309 GeV for stops, and 562 GeV for gluinos, with the paper noting that these were the most stringent limits available at the time.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a high-energy physics search study, not an education study, and it does not evaluate any educational intervention or learner outcome. There is no relevant educational methodology to appraise under the requested framework.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct or indirect impact on K-12 educational practice, outcomes, or systems. It provides no evidence that could inform expectations for Khanmigo or similar education technologies.
